title: Praying for the dead
hookLine: the living pray for the dead, and the Qur'an is recited for them in many communities

cards: A man came to the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, worried about his mother. She had died suddenly, he said, and he thought that if she'd had the chance to speak, she would have given something in charity.

So: if I give charity for her now, will it reach her? The Prophet said yes. 'A'ishah tells it, in Sahih al-Bukhari. A son, too late for one last conversation, asking if there's still a way to do something for her.

teach.b: That yes is the floor this day stands on: in Islam, the living can still do something for the dead.
The first thing, the one anyone can do, is du'a, a personal prayer asking God for them. The Qur'an gives words for it.
In surah Ibrahim, the prophet Abraham prays, in Pickthall's translation: "Our Lord! Forgive me and my parents and believers on the day when the account is cast."
And in surah al-Hashr, those who came later in the faith say: "Our Lord! Forgive us and our brethren who were before us in the faith." Me, my parents, the believers, the ones who went before.
The prayer holds the whole line at once. The funeral prayer is itself a du'a for the one who died. The greeting at the graves asks well-being for the dead.
And yesterday's hadith counts a child's prayer among the things that keep reaching a person. Then there's the Qur'an recited for the dead.
In some communities, people gather after a death to recite, and some read surah Ya Sin.

Here the scholars have differed. Some hold that the reward of recitation can be given to the dead and reaches them. Others hold to what the hadith name directly, such as du'a and charity, and are cautious about more.
Both views draw on the texts, and on love for the dead. The plainest part is shared by both: remember them, and ask God for them.

how: Muslims make du'a for their dead, using words like those in Qur'an 14:41 and 59:10, and give charity in their names; in some communities people also gather to recite the Qur'an, sometimes surah Ya Sin, though scholars differ on whether the reward of recitation reaches the dead.

games.q: what does “praying for the dead” mean?
o: a yearly prayer the family must hold on the day of the death
the funeral prayer alone, said once at the burial and never again
du'a and charity offered for the dead, which can still reach them

p: our brethren who were before us

s: in Islam, nothing the living do can reach the dead

all scholars agree that the reward of reciting Qur'an reaches the dead

games.q: your mother died suddenly, and you think she'd have wanted to give charity. what do you ask?
o: is it too late to do anything for her?
if I give charity for her, will it reach her?
should I just try to forget it?
games.why: in al-Bukhari, the man asks just that, and the Prophet answers yes.

practice: Let one person who has died come to mind, say their name quietly, and remember one specific thing about them: a laugh, a phrase, a meal.

If you pray, you can use Abraham's words from surah Ibrahim, Our Lord, forgive me and my parents and the believers, or the words from al-Hashr for those who were before us. If you don't pray, simply remember them with care.
